title: add difficulty-calibrator-and-heuristic-resampler-ci-hook
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Adds a prompt difficulty calibration module and a CI gate that detects and rejects regressions attributable to shifts in prompt difficulty. Includes a heuristic resampler to rebalance prompt cohorts and a docs page describing knob settings and rollout guidance.
description: Motivation: CI quality gates have been vulnerable to false positives/negatives when prompt sets shift subtly in difficulty (length, novelty vs. anchor set, generation entropy). This PR introduces a difficulty-calibrator component that scores prompts by a composite difficulty metric and a heuristic resampler used both during local eval runs and as a CI hook to detect distributional shifts. What changed: 1) eval_harness/difficulty/calibrator.py: new module that computes a composite difficulty score per prompt (token-length-normalized surprisal proxy from a lightweight LM scoring pass, embedding distance to anchored prompt centroids, and response-model entropy estimate). 2) eval_harness/ci/hooks/difficulty_gate.py: CI hook that compares the baseline difficulty distribution (stored as a short histogram blob in CI artifacts) to the current run using a K-S style test plus a shift-aware regression control. 3) eval_harness/samplers/heuristic_resampler.py: on-disk reweighting/resampling strategy to rebalance evaluation batches by difficulty quintiles and optionally prioritize historically unstable prompts. 4) tests/*: unit tests and small integration smoke tests. 5) docs/eval/difficulty_calibrator.md: design doc and recommended thresholds for CI. Design notes / how it works: - Composite difficulty score is a weighted sum (configurable) of:  a) normalized surprisal estimate (fast model-forward on a small ngram LM checkpoint)  b) semantic novelty (embedding cosine distance to nearest 50-anchor prompts)  c) response entropy proxy derived from prewired model-forward token logits for a short rollout. - The CI hook computes two signals: (A) distributional shift score (K-S on difficulty scalar) and (B) difficulty-conditioned regression delta: prompts are bucketed into quintiles and the primary quality metric (e.g., F1/ROUGE/semantic-sim) is compared per-bin to baseline; the hook fails only if either (1) the overall shift exceeds a tunable threshold AND the difficulty-conditioned per-bin regression exceeds per-bin thresholds OR (2) there is a significant regression concentrated in a bin with low sample count that cannot be explained by sampling variance. - The heuristic resampler reweights the eval queue to match a target difficulty distribution (default: baseline quintile proportions) and includes an 'attenuate-hotspots' option to avoid repeatedly exposing the same unstable prompts. Testing & CI: - Added deterministic-seed tests for calibrator computations and a small simulated-run integration test that exercises the gate with contrived baseline/current distributions. - CI initially failed on test_rebalance_sample due to non-determinism in the random seed used by the sampling smoke test; fixed by pinning RNG in the test and re-running. - Full pipeline (unit + smoke + lint) passed on rerun. Rollout plan: - Enabled as opt-in in CI for 1 week (flag: ci.enable_difficulty_gate=false by default). After observing false positive rate <1% on main branch historical windows and one week of canary on the release/* lanes, flip to opt-out. - Ops/Oncall runbook section added in docs describing how to interpret per-bin regressions and how to backfill baseline histograms. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op unless baseline artifact present and ci flag enabled; no breaking changes to public APIs.

small_diff_snippets:
+++ eval_harness/difficulty/calibrator.py
+def score_prompt(prompt, anchors, lm, embedder, cfg):
+    # fast surprisal approx + embedding novelty + entropy proxy
+    s = lm.fast_surprisal(prompt) / max(1, len(prompt.split()))
+    e = 1 - max_cosine_similarity(embedder.embed(prompt), anchors)
+    h = lm.response_entropy_proxy(prompt, rollout=cfg.rollout_steps)
+    return cfg.alpha * s + cfg.beta * e + cfg.gamma * h
review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice approach. A few questions: 1) how sensitive is the composite score to the LM used for surprisal? We should document the recommended small LM and provide a fallback. 2) Can we avoid storing full histograms in CI artifacts (size concerns)? Consider bucketing to quintiles / small sketch.

Priya Rao (author): Answered — surprisal uses a small distilled 125M LM by default; configuration allows swapping to a larger model if teams prefer higher fidelity. Histograms are stored as 5-quintile counts by default to cap size; full-precision debug blobs are kept only when ci.debug=true.
Marta Gonzalez: Request change — add a deterministic seed to the resampler smoke test. Also, please add a short note in docs on how threshold values were selected (calibration run).
Priya Rao: Addressed — pinned RNG in tests and added calibration note under 'Selecting thresholds' in docs/eval/difficulty_calibrator.md. Updated tests and docs in follow-up commit.
Samuel Lee: Approve after comments addressed. Concern: ops runbook should include a quick mitigation (e.g., temporarily disable gate) — please add this to docs.
Priya Rao: Added runbook mitigation steps in docs and included the ci flag for rapid disable.

notes_for_oncall: If a quality CI failure is labeled 'difficulty-shifted-quality-regression', check the per-quintile delta report attached to the CI artifact. If regressions are concentrated in high-difficulty quintiles, consider: 1) re-running evaluations with the heuristic_resampler to increase sample size, 2) temporarily disabling the gate by setting ci.enable_difficulty_gate=false in the CI config, 3) filing SUP ticket with dataset and run ids to request a manual triage. Baseline histograms can be backfilled using 'eval_harness/tools/backfill_baseline --from-run <run-id>'.
